DC-2025-B260838.aiSummary: The bill would symbolically name the 1500 block of 45th Street NE, between Douglass Street NE and Quarles Street NE in Ward 7, as "Kentrell Devaughn Way." documents.label: Notice of Public Hearing filed in the Office of Secretary by Judiciary and Publ…

DC-2025-B260618.aiSummary: The bill would require D.C. police to record key details about every officer at an arrest scene, including names or badge numbers, whether any force was used, and how many officers did not identify themselves. It would also require the Mayor to release certain body camera video and a short incident description within 5 business days after a serious use of force by a federal officer, when D.C. police body cameras captured part of the event. The bill defines a federal law enforcement officer and would apply after approval, congressional review, and publication.

B26-0827 Introduced by Councilmember Lewis George at Office of the Secretary

DC-2025-B260827.aiSummary: The act would let District residents apply for a block party permit to close a street for a Porchfest, which is a neighborhood music festival on private property or nearby public space with no fee. It also adds Porchfest to the District’s block party rules and says the District should approve block parties, including Porchfests. The emergency act became law and lasts for no more than 90 days.

DC-2025-B260016.aiSummary: The law creates a program where certain groups, like businesses, nonprofits, and some event organizers, can ask for extra parking enforcement and pay the city back for it. It also lets campus police issue parking tickets in certain areas tied to their schools, if the school gives notice and the officer has training that matches the city’s rules. The District must also set rules for tracking tickets and handling how the money from these tickets is shared.

It would spell out that the medical director oversees clinical parts of pre-hospital emergency medical services, including dispatch rules and quality checks. It would also require OUC call takers and dispatchers to get Emergency Medical Dispatch certification within one year of being hired, or within one year after the act takes effect for current staff.

DC-2025-B260038.aiSummary: The bill would let the District’s Clemency Board waive the five-year waiting period for people seeking a pardon, but only if the federal Pardon Attorney or the President has already given that person a waiver. It would apply to pardon applicants who ask for the waiver, and the Board could still deny it. The Board could not grant a waiver to someone on probation, parole, or supervised release.

DC-2025-B260816.aiSummary: The bill would make technical updates to the rules for the D.C. Public Library and its Board of Library Trustees. It would update old job titles, let the board elect its chair every two years, and treat the library’s answers to Council oversight questions as its annual report. It would also spell out how the board can handle permits, fees, and fee waivers for private revenue-making use of library property.

DC-2025-B260863.title: Mayoral Transition Emergency Amendment Act of 2026

actions.text: Transmitted to Mayor, Response Due on Nov 12, 2026
Retained by the Council
Final Reading
B26-0863 Introduced by Chairman Mendelson at Office of the Secretary

DC-2025-B260863.aiSummary: This emergency bill would update District rules so a transition committee can be set up for the Mayor-elect and use the same meaning of "Mayor-elect" in related rules. It defines "Mayor-elect" as the person certified as the winner of the 2026 mayoral election, or before that the unofficial winner if the margin is at least 2%. If approved, it would take effect right away and stay in place for up to 90 days.
